documentation.title: Large sliding: the mortar partition follows the surface too
documentation.description:
Gate for the mortar partition under slidingType="large", and the companion of ContactSlidingRamp2d. That testcase gates the PAIRING; this one gates the PARTITION, a separate mechanism that used to be a separate defect.
Why they differ. The mortar sub-cells are cut along the projected outlines of the primary elements, and those outlines move relative to a sliding secondary element, so a partition built once at setup stops lining up with the boundaries it was cut along. The points are still paired correctly and still report the right gap -- so nothing in the reported geometry looks wrong -- but their integration WEIGHTS again span more than one primary element, which is precisely the Gauss-point-to-segment error that mortar segmentation exists to remove.
GEOMETRY. The primary surface is a shallow symmetric tent of FOUR straight LINE3 faces. The two boundaries away from the apex are the point of the mesh: they are element boundaries on a STRAIGHT part of the surface, so crossing one changes nothing a point can see -- same height, same normal -- and everything about how the secondary element has to be cut. That separates the partition from the pairing cleanly, which the apex does not. The secondary surface is one LINE3 given a rigid tangential displacement of 0.7 in x, with applyContactForce="no", so nothing depends on an elasticity solution and every number is arithmetic on the mesh.
THE ASSERTION is discrete, and it is three counts rather than one:
numCells 2 -> 3 numPoints 4 -> 6 numContactElements 2 -> 3
A partition frozen on the reference configuration reports 2, 4 and 2 in the deformed state. It cannot report anything else: it was cut before the body moved.
minGap is reported alongside and differs by only about 1.6 % from the stale-partition value, which is exactly why this defect is worth a discrete assertion: the gap is nearly right even when the partition is wrong, because it depends on the pairing and the pairing is refreshed either way. integratedArea is the control -- a partition is a partition of the SAME surface however it is cut.
